findings.location: example 'creates exactly one row across duplicate deliveries and does not raise' (lines 111-118)
findings.title: Duplicate-delivery test is vacuous with respect to the uniqueness invariant: it still passes with the conversion guard AND the partial unique index both deleted, because the pre-existing 5-minute dedupe blocks the second delivery
findings.detail: The test performs the two invoice.paid deliveries back-to-back within the same example, so the second CreateSubscriptionEvent.call carries byte-identical event_params (event_type 'trial_converted_to_paid', from_plan nil, to_plan 'plan_ats_tier_starter_v2', stripe_subscription_id, amount 4900) and lands inside the pre-existing recent_duplicate window (create_subscription_event.rb: organization.subscription_events.where(event_params).where('created_at >= ?', 5.minutes.ago)). Delete conversion_duplicate_exists?, its call site, AND idx_subscription_events_conversion_stripe_sub_id: the 5-minute dedupe still context.fail!s the second call, Interactor .call swallows the failure, the webhook's begin/rescue sees no raise, count changes by exactly 1, and every assertion passes. The test therefore verifies pre-existing within-window redelivery behavior, not the new invariant; the invariant's distinct value is precisely the beyond-5-minute duplicate (renewal invoice a month later, redelivery hours later), which no webhook-level test exercises. Violates SPEC §9.3's no-ghost-tests clause / pipeline rule 26 for the named uniqueness assertion. Note: the interactor-level tests ARE non-vacuous (the cross-type guard examples use differing event_types that dodge the dedupe; the RecordNotUnique backstop stubs conversion_duplicate_exists? false and dies with the index deleted), so the invariant machinery is falsifiably tested in isolation — but the end-to-end duplicate-delivery test named by §9.1 cannot detect deletion of the feature.
findings.suggested_fix: Between the two deliveries, push the first conversion row out of the dedupe window (e.g., SubscriptionEvent.last.update_column(:created_at, 6.minutes.ago), or travel 6.minutes around the second delivery). Then the second delivery is blocked only by the conversion guard/index, and the change-by-1 assertion fails if the invariant is deleted.
